title: Allow Line Chart widget to hide trailing zeros in Y-axis when value is an integer to save space
line: Chart widgets now label their Y axis "8 GiB" instead of "8.0 GiB" when the value is a whole number.
explanation: The line and bar chart faces format their Y axis labels with the generic formatter, which always uses one decimal once a larger prefix such as GiB is chosen. A range up to 8 GiB therefore read 8.0, 6.0, 4.0, 2.0 GiB, wasting width in small widgets. A new formatValueCompact helper in the QML Formatter shows whole numbers without decimals, and both chart faces use it for their axis labels; fractional values keep their decimal.

commits.message:
faces: drop trailing zeros from whole numbers in chart axis labels

The Y axis labels of the line and bar chart faces always showed one
decimal once a larger prefix was used, so a range up to 8 GiB read
"8.0 GiB" and wasted space. Whole numbers are now shown without decimals.

BUG: 514223

 #include "Formatter.h"
 
+#include <cmath>
+
 namespace KSysGuard
 {
 QString FormatterWrapper::formatValue(const QVariant &value, KSysGuard::Unit unit, KSysGuard::MetricPrefix targetPrefix)
@@ -25,6 +27,13 @@ QString FormatterWrapper::formatValueWithPrecision(const QVariant &value, KSysGu
     return Formatter::formatValue(value, unit, MetricPrefixAutoAdjust, FormatOptionShowNull, precision);
 }
 
+QString FormatterWrapper::formatValueCompact(const QVariant &value, KSysGuard::Unit unit)

media.caption: Line chart with Y range 0-8 GiB: labels read 8.0 GiB, 6.0 GiB, ...
Same widget with the fix: 8 GiB, 6 GiB, 4 GiB, 2 GiB

review.text: Small and contained: a QML formatter helper that drops the decimal only for whole numbers, used only for the line and bar chart axis labels, so live values elsewhere keep fixed width. It reuses Formatter's existing scaleDownFactor and precision handling, and the screenshot shows 8/6/4/2 GiB as asked. Only nit is the barchart call's continuation line now being misaligned by one column.
